title: Surface tension
caption: Molecules inside a liquid are pulled equally in all directions by their neighbours; molecules at the surface are pulled only sideways and inwards. The surface behaves like a stretched skin, strongest in water because of hydrogen bonding.
alt: Water molecules in a beaker; those at the surface have neighbours only beside and below them.
description: Molecules in the bulk are surrounded on every side.
Surface molecules have no neighbours above, so they are pulled inwards.
